name: ct_trauma_pan_scan
scan_type: CT trauma pan-scan (head, cervical spine, chest, abdomen, pelvis with contrast)
clinical_history: 27M motorcyclist vs car at speed. GCS 14 at scene, now 15. Transient hypotension responding to fluids. Chest wall crepitus, pelvic binder in situ. Trauma protocol.
findings:
- Right frontal thin acute subdural haematoma, 4mm, no midline shift
- No cervical spine fracture or malalignment
- Right pneumothorax, moderate, chest drain not yet sited
- Right 3rd to 7th rib fractures, segmental 4th and 5th
- Right pulmonary contusions
- No aortic injury, mediastinal contour normal
- Grade III splenic laceration with subcapsular haematoma and focal active arterial blush
- Moderate haemoperitoneum
- Liver, kidneys, pancreas intact
- Undisplaced right superior and inferior pubic rami fractures, SI joints intact
- L1 superior endplate compression fracture, no retropulsion
- Bladder intact on delayed phase, no contrast extravasation

name: ct_pancreatic_ca_staging
scan_type: CT pancreas protocol (arterial and portal venous phases)
clinical_history: 68F painless jaundice, 8kg weight loss, bilirubin 180, CA19-9 1200. Staging for suspected pancreatic malignancy.
findings:
- 3.4cm hypoenhancing mass in pancreatic head and uncinate process
- Double duct sign: CBD 15mm, pancreatic duct 6mm with abrupt cut-off
- Mass abuts SMV over approximately 190 degrees with focal narrowing, not occluded
- SMA fat plane preserved, contact less than 90 degrees
- Coeliac axis and hepatic artery clear
- Two hypoenhancing liver lesions, segment VI 8mm and segment VII 11mm, suspicious for metastases
- Portacaval and peripancreatic nodes, largest 13mm short axis
- Duodenal wall involvement at D2
- No peritoneal nodularity or ascites
- Lung bases clear

name: mri_brain_mets_haemorrhage
clinical_history: 54F known ER+ breast cancer on letrozole. Two weeks of headaches, acute confusion and vomiting this morning.
findings:
- Four enhancing lesions: right cerebellar 28mm, left frontal 12mm, right parietal 9mm, left occipital 6mm
- Right cerebellar lesion contains acute haemorrhage with fluid-fluid level
- Marked cerebellar oedema with effacement of the fourth ventricle
- Early obstructive hydrocephalus, temporal horns dilated
- 5mm tonsillar descent
- No leptomeningeal enhancement
- Supratentorial lesions show moderate perilesional oedema, no midline shift
- No restricted diffusion to suggest infarct
- Dural venous sinuses patent

name: mri_spine_mscc
clinical_history: 72M metastatic prostate cancer, PSA 85. Three weeks progressive thoracic back pain, 48 hours bilateral leg weakness with two falls, new urinary hesitancy. Query cord compression.
findings:
- Multilevel vertebral metastases at C7, T3, T7, T9, L2 and L4
- T7 posterior vertebral body and pedicle involvement with epidural soft tissue component
- Epidural disease at T7 compresses the cord, with high T2 cord signal at this level
- Greater than 50% canal compromise at T7
- T9 epidural disease abuts the cord without compression
- Conus normal, no cauda equina compromise
- T7 vertebral height loss 30% with 15 degrees kyphosis
- L4 pathological fracture, no retropulsion
- Paraspinal soft tissue mass at T7 extending to the costovertebral junctions

name: ct_necrotising_pancreatitis
clinical_history: 49M alcohol excess. Admitted 6 days ago with severe epigastric pain, amylase 2100. Persistent fever, CRP rising to 320 despite antibiotics. Day 6 assessment.
findings:
- Non-enhancement of over 50% of pancreatic body and tail, consistent with necrosis
- Pancreatic head and uncinate enhance normally
- Large acute necrotic collection in lesser sac, 9 x 5cm, extending down left paracolic gutter
- No gas within collections
- Splenic vein thrombosis with early perigastric varices
- Portal vein patent
- Moderate left pleural effusion with basal atelectasis
- Gallbladder normal, no radio-opaque gallstones, CBD normal calibre
- Kidneys enhance symmetrically
- No free intraperitoneal gas
